sentences.text:
Despite service of notice, none appears for respondent No.1.
2.

Questioning the validity of the order that is rendered by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-VI Vijayapur in MVC No.927/2015 dated 14.09.2018 (common order), the present appeal is filed by the claimants.

3. Undisputedly, the first appellant is the wife and rest of the appellants are the children of the deceased Somaning Chowkande (hereinafter referred to as the "deceased" for brevity) who died in the road traffic accident that occurred on 23.06.2014.

The case of the appellants is that on the date mentioned above, the deceased along with appellant Nos.1, 4 and his relative by name Sridevi was proceeding on a Hero Honda Shine Motorcycle from Jangalagi to Salagar and at that time, one Commander jeep bearing registration No.MH-13/N-3911 which was coming in NC:
2024:KHC-K:624-DB the opposite direction being driver by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the motorcycle, due to which the deceased and others fell down.
The deceased and Sridevi succumbed to the injuries.
Appellant Nos.1 and 4 sustained injuries.
4. The appellants through this appeal exhibited their grievance with regard to the quantum that is awarded as compensation.

5. Making his submission, the learned counsel for the appellants states that as against the claim for Rs.50,00,000/-, the tribunal awarded a paltry sum of Rs.10,54,200/- as compensation and the same is highly unjustifiable.
The counsel on record for respondent No.2 is also heard in this regard.

6. A perusal of the impugned order goes to show that the tribunal, taking the notional income of the deceased @ Rs.6,000/- per month, proceeded with the computation of compensation and arrived at a figure.
As per the version of the appellants, the deceased was doing business and agriculture was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
However, as rightly observed by the tribunal, no proof is produced to that effect.
Yet undisputedly as per the contents of Ex.
P5 - post mortem report, the deceased was aged about 32 years by the date of the accident.
The accident occurred in the year 2014.

Therefore, this Smt. Vidyashree W/O Somaning Chougule ... vs Sau Ayesha W/O Rafiq Khatib And Anr on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178303968/
3
Court is of the view that the tribunal ought to have taken the nominal income of the deceased as Rs.7,500/- per month.
Further more, as rightly contended no future prospects are added.
3 Towards loss of estate Rs.15,000/-

4 Towards loss of consortium Rs.20,000/-
 5 Towards Funeral Expenses Rs.15,000/-
The observation of the tribunal that the father and mother of the deceased are also entitled for compensation requires no interference.
Also it is borne by NC: 2024:KHC-K:624-DB record that the father and mother of the deceased filed MVC No.2201/2014 and they were also awarded compensation along with the appellants herein.
Thus, the dependants are seven in number.

In case,
the income of the deceased is taken as Rs.7,500/- and future prospects @ 40% is added as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, the monthly income of the deceased comes to Rs.10,500/-.

entities.text: National Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The annual income thus is Rs.1,26,000/-.
9.

Having considered the fact that the dependants are seven in number, 1/5th of the income of the deceased has to be deducted towards the personal and living expenses which the deceased would have incurred for himself had he been alive.
Thus, the contribution of the deceased towards the appellants as well as his parents comes to Rs.1,00,800/.
The appropriate multiplier to be is 16.

Thus, the loss of dependency comes to Rs.16,12,800/-
NC: 2024:KHC-K:624-DB 10.

As the dependants are the parents, wife and four minor children aged 9 years, 7 years, 3 years,
and 6 months by the date of the accident, this Court considers desirable to award a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- in total as loss of consortium.
Together with the said amount the dependants are also entitled to Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate.

Hence, the amount which the appellants and the parents of the deceased who are the claimants in MVC No.2201/2014 are entitled to as compensation is as under:

 2 Towards loss of estate Rs.15,000/-

(iii) The enhanced amount carries interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
(iv) The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the enhanced amount within a period of eight weeks.
(v) The apportionment made by the tribunal in respect of the appellants as well as in respect of the claimants in MVC No.2201/2014 remains undisturbed.
